messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — GeoDNS / external resolver anomaly detected for inference.redwood.com. Alerts: high NXDOMAIN + timeout rate from EU/UK resolvers, spike in 5xxs for customers routed to eu-west-1 pool. Pager: @jordan. Initial metric summary: 4.7% errors (5m), median latency +120ms (5m), per-region divergence in health checks.

jordan: On it — collecting facts. Which upstreams are flapping?

maya: Route53 health checks for eu-west-1 are flapping (HTTP 503 / timeout) starting ~2043012200. Cloudflare resolver logs show increased SERVFAILs and timeouts from several EU PoPs. Not all users affected — appears to be resolver/regional path problem.

leo: Confirming from our DNS probes: dig +trace inference.redwood.com from eu-west returns DEPRECATED region ip set (old pool) sometimes, and sometimes times out entirely. Running continuous probe now.

alex: Quick mitigation options: (1) reduce TTL to 30s for the record so changes propagate faster; (2) enable geo-fallback routing to prefer healthy east/west pools; (3) if Route53 health checks are noisy, temporarily set manual overrides to pin traffic to healthy pool. I can run 2+3 if we agree.

jordan: Agree with short TTL + manual override. Need product impact summary before we change routing. Sarah, can you pull the customer impact list?

sarah: Pulling. Preliminary: 6 customer tenants showing elevated 5xxs (inference calls failing) concentrated in EU customers; a few enterprise customers on dedicated capacity hit timeouts for webhooks. Estimated ~3–5% of total requests. Logging shows errors are backend timeouts rather than model decode failures.

alex: Command snippets I'm about to run:
```
# lower TTL on Route53 record (change record-set TTL)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZABCDEFGHI --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.com.","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.12.34.56"}]}}]}'

# apply geo-fallback policy (manual override) via our internal geodns console
# UI action: Override eu-west allocation -> point at fallback pool (eu-fallback-01)
```

jordan: Go ahead with TTL + manual override. Notify customers and open tickets with CF and AWS. Keep change window minimal. Post each change here.

alex: Lowered TTL to 30s at 2043012405 UTC (prop change submitted, Route53 change id change-XYZ). Expecting propagation within 30s–120s depending on caches.

maya: Route53 health checks still flapping; I'm disabling the automated failover from health-check triggers to prevent oscillation while we stabilize. Doing that now.

leo: Manual override applied at 2043012460 UTC — eu routes now point to eu-fallback-01 (healthy). Running live probes — dropping NXDOMAIN count in probes.

support-bot: Opened internal customer incident thread: INC-2043, notified account teams for impacted customers (list attached).

jordan: Contacting Cloudflare & AWS support:
- CF ticket opened (CF#20240301-9843) — reported SERVFAIL/timeouts from EU PoPs.
- AWS case opened for Route53 health-check flapping (AWS#987654321).

alex: Observability update: 1m after override, EU error rate down from 4.7% -> 0.9%. Latency trending down. Still seeing a handful of resolver timeouts — likely caches needing to expire.

sarah: Customer comms draft: short status message saying we're experiencing regional DNS resolver errors affecting some EU customers; mitigation in progress; ETA 30–60m. Want to publish to status.redwood.com?

jordan: Publish — keep wording conservative and include workaround: restart clients / retry after 1 minute. Also add note about TTL change so customers know DNS may be unstable briefly.

maya: From packet captures — some EU resolvers are returning truncated UDP responses leading to TCP fallback and timeouts; looks like a resolver-side issue (CF edge or peering). Cloudflare rep acknowledged investigating CF#20240301-9843.

leo: Handing off oncall to @leo (taking over) — jordan out at 2043012800 UTC for 30m. Summary for handoff: TTL lowered to 30, manual override to eu-fallback-01 applied, Route53 health-checks disabled for flapping prevention, CF & AWS tickets open. Watch for reversion and propagation.

leo: Oncall ack. Monitoring probes show stable for last 3 mins. I'll keep 1:1 probes running and coordinate with CF engineer if they request dig traces.

alex: FYI I'll keep the manual override for another 30m while CF and AWS investigate. If everything looks good at +30m, we'll roll traffic back and restore original TTL (300s).

support-bot: Notified customers (enterprise owners + status page updated). Public status message posted at 2043012912 UTC.

jordan: Rejoined briefly — thanks team. Postmortem action items (quick):
- Add automated detection playbook for DNS resolver truncation -> auto-failover to fallback pool.
- Improve health-check noise filtering to avoid Route53 oscillation.
- Add synthetic probes from multiple EU ISPs to detect resolver-level truncation.
- Track CF ticket resolution & attach to incident.

leo: Will monitor for 30m then either revert override + raise TTL back to 300 or escalate if CF/AWS indicate longer fix. Reopening thread if errors exceed 1% again.

incident-bot: Incident status updated to MONITORING. Severity downgraded to SEV3 at 2043013065.

jordan: Great work. Leaving notes in INC-2043. Closing Slack active coordination unless status changes.

leo: Closing loop here — continued monitoring, will file follow-up postmortem with logs and dig traces.
